# Rollout Plan: Migrating 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing to New Billing System

## Overview

Both billing systems will run in parallel (dual-run) throughout the migration. Users are migrated in batches; the legacy system remains fully operational as a fallback until all users are confirmed stable on the new system for a defined soak period. No teardown of the legacy system occurs until after the final migration batch has passed its stability window.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (2% of users — ~800 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed a full end-to-end test suite (invoicing, proration, refunds, tax calculation, payment retries) in staging with 100% parity against legacy outputs on a replayed sample of 5,000 historical transactions, AND a rollback procedure has been tested successfully in staging.

- Select low-risk, internal/beta-friendly accounts (employees, design partners, opted-in beta users) plus a small random sample.
- Run both systems in parallel per user (shadow billing): new system generates invoices/charges that are compared against legacy output but legacy remains authoritative for actual charges initially, then cut over to new-system-as-authoritative for this cohort after 48 hours of clean shadow comparison.
- Monitor daily for 5–7 business days minimum before proceeding.

## Phase 2: Expansion (25% of users — ~10,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed its full soak period (7 days) with zero unresolved critical billing discrepancies, error rate and financial-drift metrics below halt thresholds (see below), and support ticket volume from Phase 1 cohort not exceeding 1.5x baseline.

- Migrate in daily sub-batches (e.g., ~1,500–2,000/day) segmented by customer tier, geography, and plan complexity to surface edge cases (multi-currency, enterprise contracts, coupons/discounts) progressively.
- Continue dual-run/shadow reconciliation for each sub-batch for 48 hours before treating the new system as authoritative for that sub-batch.
- Weekly go/no-go review with finance, support, and engineering stakeholders.

## Phase 3: General Availability (73% of remaining users — ~29,200 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 fully soaked (minimum 10 days cumulative) with all halt-metric thresholds green across every customer segment migrated so far, finance sign-off on reconciliation accuracy, and support team confirmed adequately staffed/trained for full-scale cutover volume.

- Migrate remaining users in larger daily batches (e.g., 10–15% of total user base per day), prioritizing simpler accounts first and the most complex/high-revenue enterprise accounts last.
- Maintain dual-run reconciliation for each batch for a minimum 48-hour window before authoritative cutover.
- Legacy system remains live, read-accessible, and capable of processing charges as a fallback for any user rolled back during this phase.

## Phase 4: Legacy Decommission (0% of users — infrastructure only, no user migration occurs in this phase)

**Entry criterion:** 100% of users successfully migrated and authoritative on the new system for a minimum continuous soak period of 30 days with no reconciliation discrepancies, all financial close/audit cycles for that period completed and signed off by finance/accounting, and full data archival of legacy system verified and restorable.

- Disable write access to legacy billing system first (read-only archive mode) before any deletion.
- Decommission legacy infrastructure only after archival is independently verified restorable.

---

## Risks

RISK: Financial discrepancies between old and new systems cause incorrect customer charges or revenue leakage | Run mandatory 48-hour dual-run shadow reconciliation per batch with automated diffing before authoritative cutover; require finance sign-off per phase | Finance/Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: Migration script or data mapping errors corrupt customer payment methods or subscription state | Use idempotent, dry-run-capable migration jobs with per-user rollback snapshots taken before migration | Platform Engineering Lead
RISK: Support team overwhelmed by billing-related tickets during large batches, delaying issue detection | Stagger batch sizes, pre-train support staff per phase, and set ticket-volume circuit breakers tied to batch pacing | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Enterprise/high-complexity accounts (multi-currency, custom contracts) migrated too early cause high-value billing errors | Sequence migration so complex/high-revenue accounts are migrated last, only after simpler cohorts prove stable | Enterprise Accounts Lead
RISK: Legacy system decommissioned prematurely, eliminating fallback before new system is fully validated | Enforce hard gate requiring 30-day full-population soak and archival verification before any decommission step | VP Engineering / Program Owner

---

## Halt Metrics

Rollout must **pause immediately** and trigger incident review if any of the following occur for an active batch or cohort:

- **Billing discrepancy rate > 0.5%** of migrated transactions (dollar-amount mismatch between old and new system outputs) in any 24-hour window.
- **Failed/declined payment rate increases by more than 20% relative** to that cohort's pre-migration baseline within 48 hours of cutover.
- **Critical (Sev1/Sev2) billing incidents ≥ 2** within any single rolling 24-hour period tied to the new system.
- **Customer support ticket volume for billing issues exceeds 1.5x baseline** for the affected cohort for more than 24 hours.

Any single threshold breach halts further migration into new batches; already-migrated users may be rolled back to legacy processing per the tested rollback procedure while root cause is investigated.

PHASES: 4
